newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian aluminium plants to contain output.
newsitem.headline: Russian aluminium plants to contain output.

text.p: Russia's aluminium producers have agreed not to increase output from current levels, but will not make cuts in existing production levels, the chief executive of the Kontsern Alyuminiy producers' association said on Monday.

"There is no agreement to cut output, but there is an agreement, taken at board level at the smelters, not to bring on line new capacity that is not now being used," said Igor Prokopov, adding that 80,000-100,000 tonnes of currently unused capacity would not be activated.
"As far as I know, some other countries have agreed to do the same," said Prokopov.
"That the market is not healthy is evident to everyone," said Vladimir Kalchenko, Kontsern Aluminiy first deputy chief executive, told Reuters.
"We should first and foremost stop cultivating the development, the further development, of new capacities."
Industry specialists Anthony Bird and Associates last week estimated current capacity at leading smelters Bratsk, Krasnoyarsk and Sayansk at 850,000, 810,000 and 270,000 tonnes, respectively.
Prokopov said Russian government officials had agreed to share statistical information on output with other major international producers.
A two-year global deal to reduce output by 10 percent was signed in March 1994 by major producers Russia, Australia, Canada, the European Union, Norway and the United States and ended this spring.
Under the memorandum of understanding (MOU) -- designed to tackle a world glut and bloated inventories -- Russia's annualised output cuts were 150,000 tonnes in early 1995 and 280,000 tonnes in 1994.
Kontsern Alyuminiy has said that Russian output of primary aluminium over January-August was 1.88 million tonnes, a 2.3 percent rise on 1995 levels.

State Customs Committee figures put Russia's January-August aluminium exports outside the Commonwealth of Independent States at over 1.75 million tonnes. --Lynnley Browning, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
